gaps.explanation: 'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.

gaps.sentence: She gave me some useful ___ about buying a house.
gaps.hint: a noun is needed after 'some useful'
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is the uncountable noun; 'advise' is the verb. 'Advices' is not standard English.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.
'You're' is short for 'you are'; 'your' shows possession.

gaps.sentence: I couldn't ___ what he was saying because of the noise.
gaps.explanation: 'Hear' means to receive sound; 'listen' means to pay attention deliberately and needs 'to'.

gaps.sentence: The country is facing a serious ___ crisis.
gaps.hint: connected with money, trade and industry
gaps.explanation: 'Economic' means connected with the economy; 'economical' means saving money.

gaps.sentence: We ___ money by cycling to work instead of driving.
gaps.hint: to keep money instead of spending it
gaps.explanation: 'Save money by doing something' means to avoid spending it; 'earn' means to receive money for work.

gaps.hint: past participle after 'have'; the verb takes no object
gaps.explanation: 'Rise' (rise, rose, risen) takes no object: sales have risen. 'Raise' takes an object: they raised prices.
